task_instance: Simulate a self-hosted Qdrant node hitting the RAM pressure trigger described in the skill (~80% RAM usage) with a 768-dim, 60k-vector collection running in a memory-constrained Docker container (512MiB limit), apply the skill's RAM sizing formula (num_vectors * dim * 4 bytes * 1.5) to size the target node, then perform the actual vertical scale by stopping the node and restarting it against the same storage volume with a larger memory limit (1.5GiB), and verify the collection survives intact and memory pressure drops.
evidence: Started dockerd in-sandbox and ran a real Qdrant 1.19.1 container (qdrant_small) limited to 512MiB via `docker run -m 512m --memory-swap 512m`. Loaded 60,000 vectors (dim=768) via qdrant-client; `docker stats` showed memory climbing to 82.6% (422.9MiB/512MiB) then settling around 55-78%, matching the skill's stated 'RAM usage approaching 80%' vertical-scaling trigger. Applied the skill's RAM formula: num_vectors*dim*4*1.5 = 263.7MiB full-precision estimate (scalar-quantized: 65.9MiB), consistent in order of magnitude with the observed container RSS including HNSW/WAL overhead the skill calls out. Verified `points_count: 60000` via GET /collections/docs. Performed the actual vertical scale: stopped/removed qdrant_small, started a new container (qdrant_scaled) mounting the SAME storage volume with `-m 1536m --memory-swap 1536m` (simulating a self-hosted resize, per the skill's guidance for self-hosted deployments: 'resize the underlying VM or container resources'). Confirmed data integrity post-resize (points_count still 60000, indexed_vectors_count 36000, config intact) and memory pressure resolved: `docker stats` showed 12.86% (197.5MiB/1.5GiB), down from ~80%+ before scaling. Cleaned up containers afterward (docker stop/rm qdrant_scaled); docker ps -a is empty. All work confined to the work directory; no external/paid services, no credentials, no network egress beyond the local Docker daemon and localhost HTTP calls to the container.
